industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): cyclical component makers into a growth scare, against the restock evidence in the bottom-up work: DiscoverIE's memo (Mixed) records 'the sector-wide end of destocking' and proven Stage 2 momentum while its acquisition funding fights the Fragility axis; Ericsson beat on network equipment. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: B now, B prior, the market is paying. One live holding, Volex (4.42%, Technical Momentum A, TSR/Valuation F), judged in component 4; two MI Pool names, DiscoverIE and Senior. Counter-case for higher: persistent relative strength and the restock; for lower: components are the first order cut when the margin rolls over. Balanced, so Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack this week, so the condition for B (a confidence print at or above normal with the Riksbank on hold) could not be tested; the only Swedish data point is food retail volumes up 5.3% in September after a value-added tax cut (Danske, 18 Oct), which is a sector fact, not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 0.50%, Hexatronic 4.95%, Sdiptech 5.05%, Xvivo 5.05%, 15.55 points), judged in component 4 and in amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.
